## Summary

- **The claim:** Linear — his tool for working through software-engineering decisions and problems — is beaten by "this". No criteria are given; the screenshot is the argument.
- **The screenshot (OCR):** a Flywheel graph titled **"Artifacts for CLI agents"** — 36 nodes, 1 root, sortable by Updated, shareable ("Share graph", "Copy link"). Sidebar sections: Research, Experiments, Method, Trajectory, Problems. The mapped tree: "Problem: artifacts" branching into **Decision 1** (the day-one…), **Decision 2** (the Traject…), **Decision 3** (a Problems…), **Scope** (who is it for…), **Agent side** (how does an agent…), **Authoring**, **Display** (where and with…), **Runtime** (what may an…), **Feedback**. Sibling heads visible: "Claude artifacts: feedback / sharing / permissions / tool… / source…", "Capability map: Claude…". A filter readout shows **"135 heads without status"**.
- **What Flywheel is:** Paradigma's product (Rome; @paradigmainc; flywheel.paradigma.inc) — "the infrastructure for autonomous research". Docs: research work is a **directed graph** — nodes are work units, branches are divergent paths, and merged outcomes "preserve a reviewable record of decisions and evidence". Operable by agents via **CLI + MCP** (runs in Codex, Claude Code "and everything else" — Fazio announced the CLI himself, Apr 2026), plus a Web UI, public shareable graphs, Campaigns, and a timeline view. Community framing: "git, but for science".

## Why it matters

- **The structural bet:** Linear flattens an investigation into a list of statuses; a graph keeps the branch structure AND attaches each decision to the evidence that produced it. For multi-branch work (strategy retests, reskin rollouts, agent experiments) that is the difference between a to-do list and an audit trail — the same reason this vault keeps the D. Martin arc as linked notes rather than tickets ([[2026-11-13-dmartin-unseen-years-retest]]).
- **MCP-native means agents read and write the decision graph, not just humans** — work-orchestration adjacency with [[2026-11-08-brian-armstrong-agent-org-queue]] and with structured agent planning [[2026-09-06-phelps-agentic-planning-loop]]; the graph UI itself echoes [[2026-10-19-flohoeller-agent-tree-component]], and "curated context CLI agents actually consume" is the same problem [[2026-10-18-copyconstruct-claude-md-curated-corpus]] attacks from the prompt side.
- **Skepticism gates:** the author joined Paradigma in March 2026 — this is employee dogfooding + evangelism, not a neutral Linear comparison; "better" is asserted, never defined; the screenshot shows one well-formed graph (survivorship — nobody screenshots their messy one); his own sidebar reads "135 heads without status", i.e. the status-discipline problem Linear exists to solve shows up here too; 519 likes measure audience overlap, not tool quality.
- **Actionable:** task filed — a cheap spike (free tier, CLI/MCP from Claude Code) mapping one live multi-branch item as a 5–10 node graph, judged against the flat-list + vault-note workflow.
